list.name: contributor
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT COALESCE(NULLIF(contributor, ''), '(unattributed)') AS __text, COALESCE(NULLIF(contributor, ''), '') AS __value FROM whodunit_repos ORDER BY 1
list.label: Contributor

options.content:
**What this measures, and what it does not.** These figures come from agent sessions observed on developers' own machines, so they cover only repositories where `dun init` has been run and `dun sync` has been executed.

There is no accept/reject rate here. A suggestion a developer declined never reaches the journal, so we have no denominator for it — unlike a vendor's admin API, which sees both sides. What we have instead is the link to shipped code: which commits and which lines.

panels.title: Coverage

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT w.commit_sha)
                    / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT c.sha), 0), 1) AS v
FROM commits c
JOIN repo_commits rc ON rc.commit_sha = c.sha
JOIN whodunit_commits seen ON seen.commit_sha IN (
       SELECT commit_sha FROM repo_commits WHERE repo_id = rc.repo_id)
LEFT JOIN whodunit_commits w ON w.commit_sha = c.sha
LEFT JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id = w.repo_id
WHERE ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '${contributor:raw}' OR w.commit_sha IS NULL)
  AND c.authored_date BETWEEN FROM_UNIXTIME($__unixEpochFrom())
                          AND FROM_UNIXTIME($__unixEpochTo())

panels.description:
Share of the repository's commits that carry an AI-Attribution trailer at all — instrumented or not.

**This measures instrumentation, not AI use.** A commit with `status=undetermined` counts here: it has a trailer, it just records that no agent activity was found. Adoption beside it counts only `status=assisted`.

Measured per repository: whodunit 98.9%, nj-agents 99.0%, EngageHub 79.0% — EngageHub was instrumented later, so a fifth of its history predates the hooks. Commits made before `dun init` can never be covered.

The denominator is every commit the warehouse knows about for the repository, not every commit whodunit recorded. Dividing by the latter is what made this identical to adoption.

panels.title: Active days
panels.description: Days on which any agent activity was observed. Not the same as a vendor's 'daily active users' — this counts days with recorded work, not seats logged in.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT DATE(FROM_UNIXTIME(e.observed_at / 1000000000))) AS active_days FROM whodunit_events e JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id = e.repo_id WHERE ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '${contributor:raw}') AND e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000

panels.title: Sessions
panels.description:
Agent sessions recorded in the selected range.

A session is one conversation, counted regardless of whether it produced an edit — so this measures how often an agent was opened, not how much it did. The engagement panels below separate those.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT e.session) AS sessions FROM whodunit_events e JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id = e.repo_id WHERE e.session <> '' AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '${contributor:raw}') AND e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000

panels.title: Contributors
panels.description: People whose repositories have synced. A contributor appears only after running dun sync, so this undercounts anyone using an agent without it.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT contributor) AS contributors FROM whodunit_repos WHERE contributor <> '' AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR contributor = '${contributor:raw}')

panels.title: Repositories
panels.description:
Instrumented repositories that recorded activity in range.

Only repositories where `dun init` has run appear at all: enrolment is opt-in, so this is a count of what was instrumented, not of what exists.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS repos FROM whodunit_repos WHERE ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR contributor = '${contributor:raw}')

panels.title: Lines written by agents
panels.description: Lines an agent produced across all observed edits, including work that was later rewritten or never committed. This is effort, not output — compare it with the committed figures on the attribution dashboard.

targets.rawSql: SELECT SUM(e.lines_added) AS lines_written FROM whodunit_events e JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id = e.repo_id WHERE ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '${contributor:raw}') AND e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000

panels.title: Data freshness
panels.description: Time since the last recorded agent event. The hooks write on every commit, so this tracks whether anyone has been working — green under 8 hours, amber past a working day, red past three. A long gap is a question, not a fault: a quiet weekend and a broken collector look identical here, which is why `dun verify` exists.

targets.rawSql: SELECT (UNIX_TIMESTAMP() - MAX(observed_at) / 1000000000) / 3600 AS hours_stale FROM whodunit_events

options.content:
## Did the developer keep it?

An edit an agent proposed is not an edit that shipped. These panels count what the developer **accepted**, and every rate is shown next to the count it came from — a 100% acceptance rate over 3 calls is not the same result as one over 300. `unknown` means the transcript never recorded a result (in-flight or truncated); it is never silently counted as an acceptance.

panels.title: Accepted edits
panels.description: Edit/Write calls the developer kept. This is the numerator — read it with the denominator beside it.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(*) v FROM whodunit_events e JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=e.repo_id WHERE e.outcome='accepted' AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '${contributor:raw}') AND e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000

panels.title: Decided calls
panels.description: The denominator: calls with a recorded outcome. Excludes 'unknown', so the rate is not diluted by transcripts that simply never finished.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(*) v FROM whodunit_events e JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=e.repo_id WHERE e.outcome IN ('accepted','rejected','failed') AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '${contributor:raw}') AND e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000

panels.title: Acceptance rate
panels.description: Accepted / decided. Meaningless without the denominator to its left — check that first.

targets.rawSql: SELECT ROUND(100.0*SUM(e.outcome='accepted')/NULLIF(SUM(e.outcome IN ('accepted','rejected','failed')),0),1) v FROM whodunit_events e JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=e.repo_id WHERE ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '${contributor:raw}') AND e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000

panels.title: Undecided
panels.description: Calls with no recorded result. A large number here means the rate above rests on a small slice of the work.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(*) v FROM whodunit_events e JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=e.repo_id WHERE e.outcome NOT IN ('accepted','rejected','failed') AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '${contributor:raw}') AND e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000

panels.title: Acceptance by tool
panels.description: Per tool, so a low overall rate can be traced to which one is being turned down. Rate is shown with its denominator on the same row (NAV-54).

targets.rawSql: SELECT e.tool AS `Tool`, SUM(e.outcome='accepted') AS `Accepted`, SUM(e.outcome='rejected') AS `Rejected`, SUM(e.outcome='failed') AS `Failed`, SUM(e.outcome NOT IN ('accepted','rejected','failed')) AS `Unknown`, SUM(e.outcome IN ('accepted','rejected','failed')) AS `Decided`, ROUND(100.0*SUM(e.outcome='accepted')/NULLIF(SUM(e.outcome IN ('accepted','rejected','failed')),0),1) AS `Accept %` FROM whodunit_events e JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=e.repo_id WHERE ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '${contributor:raw}') AND e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000 GROUP BY e.tool ORDER BY `Decided` DESC

panels.title: Session engagement
panels.description: How a session was actually worked, from counts only — no message text is ever recorded. 'Turns per prompt' is agent messages per human message: a high number means long autonomous runs, a low one means tight back-and-forth (NAV-55).

targets.rawSql: SELECT LEFT(s.session,8) AS `Session`, FROM_UNIXTIME(s.first_seen/1000000000) AS `Started`, ROUND((s.last_seen-s.first_seen)/60000000000) AS `Minutes`, s.user_messages AS `Prompts`, s.agent_messages AS `Agent msgs`, ROUND(s.agent_messages/NULLIF(s.user_messages,0),1) AS `Turns per prompt`, s.tool_calls AS `Tool calls`, s.distinct_tools AS `Distinct tools`, s.mcp_calls AS `MCP calls` FROM whodunit_sessions s JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=s.repo_id WHERE ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '${contributor:raw}') AND s.first_seen BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom()*1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo()*1000000000 ORDER BY s.first_seen DESC

panels.title: Agent activity over time
panels.description: Observed agent edits per day. Compare shape with the committed-work panels — a rise here without a matching rise there means iteration, not delivery.

targets.rawSql: SELECT FROM_UNIXTIME(FLOOR(e.observed_at / 1000000000 / 86400) * 86400) AS time, 'agent edits' AS metric, COUNT(*) AS value FROM whodunit_events e JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id = e.repo_id WHERE ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '${contributor:raw}') AND e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000 GROUP BY time, metric ORDER BY time

panels.title: Code churn over time
panels.description: Lines written and removed by agents per day, from observed edits rather than commits.

targets.rawSql: SELECT FROM_UNIXTIME(FLOOR(e.observed_at / 1000000000 / 86400) * 86400) AS time, 'lines added' AS metric, SUM(e.lines_added) AS value FROM whodunit_events e JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id = e.repo_id WHERE ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '${contributor:raw}') AND e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000 GROUP BY time, metric UNION ALL SELECT FROM_UNIXTIME(FLOOR(e.observed_at / 1000000000 / 86400) * 86400) AS time, 'lines removed' AS metric, SUM(e.lines_removed) AS value FROM whodunit_events e JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id = e.repo_id WHERE ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '${contributor:raw}') AND e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000 GROUP BY time, metric ORDER BY time

panels.title: Activity by tool
panels.description: Which operations agents performed. A vendor's admin API also reports how many of these a developer rejected; that is not observable here, because a rejected edit never reaches the journal.

targets.rawSql: SELECT e.tool, COUNT(*) AS events, SUM(e.lines_added) AS lines_added, SUM(e.lines_removed) AS lines_removed FROM whodunit_events e JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id = e.repo_id WHERE e.tool <> '' AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '${contributor:raw}') AND e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000 GROUP BY e.tool ORDER BY events DESC

panels.title: By agent and version
panels.description: Which agents and versions were seen. A version disappearing while activity continues usually means an adapter stopped recognising its format, not that people stopped using it.

targets.rawSql: SELECT e.agent, e.agent_version, COUNT(*) AS events, COUNT(DISTINCT e.session) AS sessions FROM whodunit_events e JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id = e.repo_id WHERE ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '${contributor:raw}') AND e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000 GROUP BY e.agent, e.agent_version ORDER BY events DESC

panels.title: By contributor
panels.description: Per-person activity. Identity comes from the git committer email already present in every commit — this makes existing information easier to query, it does not observe anything new.

targets.rawSql: SELECT r.contributor, COUNT(DISTINCT e.session) AS sessions, COUNT(*) AS agent_edits, SUM(e.lines_added) AS lines_written FROM whodunit_events e JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id = e.repo_id WHERE r.contributor <> '' AND e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000 GROUP BY r.contributor ORDER BY agent_edits DESC

panels.title: Committed work by contributor
panels.description: What reached a commit, per person — the question a vendor's usage API cannot answer. Coverage is shown alongside, because a penetration figure without it says how much of what we could see was assisted, not how much of the work was.

targets.rawSql: SELECT r.contributor, COUNT(*) AS commits, SUM(c.status = 'assisted') AS assisted, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(c.status <> 'undetermined') / COUNT(*), 0) AS coverage_pct, ROUND(AVG(c.ratio), 2) AS avg_share, SUM(c.lines_added) AS lines_added FROM whodunit_commits c JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id = c.repo_id WHERE r.contributor <> '' AND c.committed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000 GROUP BY r.contributor ORDER BY commits DESC

panels.title: Active today

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT r.contributor) v
FROM whodunit_events e JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id = e.repo_id
WHERE e.observed_at >= (UNIX_TIMESTAMP() - 1*86400) * 1000000000 AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '${contributor:raw}')

panels.description: Contributors with recorded agent activity in the last 1 day(s).

panels.title: Active this week

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT r.contributor) v
FROM whodunit_events e JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id = e.repo_id
WHERE e.observed_at >= (UNIX_TIMESTAMP() - 7*86400) * 1000000000 AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '${contributor:raw}')

panels.description: Contributors with recorded agent activity in the last 7 day(s).

panels.title: Active this month

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT r.contributor) v
FROM whodunit_events e JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id = e.repo_id
WHERE e.observed_at >= (UNIX_TIMESTAMP() - 30*86400) * 1000000000 AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '${contributor:raw}')

panels.description: Contributors with recorded agent activity in the last 30 day(s).

panels.title: Stickiness

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ROUND(
  (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT r.contributor) FROM whodunit_events e
     JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=e.repo_id
   WHERE e.observed_at >= (UNIX_TIMESTAMP() - 86400) * 1000000000 AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '${contributor:raw}')) * 100.0
  / NULLIF((SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT r.contributor) FROM whodunit_events e
     JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=e.repo_id
   WHERE e.observed_at >= (UNIX_TIMESTAMP() - 30*86400) * 1000000000 AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '${contributor:raw}')), 0), 1) v

panels.description: Daily actives as a share of monthly. High means the agent is part of the routine rather than something people tried once.

panels.title: MCP calls

targets.rawSql:
SELECT SUM(s.mcp_calls) v
FROM whodunit_sessions s JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id = s.repo_id
WHERE s.last_seen BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000 AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '${contributor:raw}')

panels.description: Calls to connected MCP servers. A total, not a breakdown: the transcripts name each server, but the collector keeps only file-editing tools today.

panels.title: Distinct tools

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT e.tool) v
FROM whodunit_events e JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id = e.repo_id
WHERE e.tool <> '' AND e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000 AND ('${contributor:raw}' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '${contributor:raw}')

panels.description: File-editing tools seen. Skills, chat and search are called as tools too and are visible in the transcripts, but are not collected yet.

panels.title: Evidence strength

targets.rawSql:
SELECT CASE c.method
         WHEN 'intersected' THEN 'intersected — the agent''s lines survived'
         WHEN 'observed'    THEN 'observed — edited before committing'
         WHEN 'declared'    THEN 'declared — stated, not measured'
         WHEN 'inferred'    THEN 'inferred — from surrounding evidence'
         ELSE 'undetermined — no evidence either way'
       END AS `method`, COUNT(*) AS `commits`
FROM whodunit_commits c JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=c.repo_id
WHERE 1=1 AND ('${contributor:raw}'='__all__' OR r.contributor='${contributor:raw}') AND c.committed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
GROUP BY c.method ORDER BY `commits` DESC

panels.description: 'undetermined' means whodunit could not tell — never that no AI was used.

options.content:
### What this dashboard cannot show *yet*

**Seats and pending invites.** Vendor billing knows who holds a licence; whodunit only knows machines it is installed on. It cannot report a seat nobody used, so adoption here is measured against people who committed — a different, smaller denominator. This one is structural.

**Which MCP server, and which skill.** The counts below are totals. The agent transcripts do name them — a call arrives as `mcp__<server>__<method>` — but the collector keeps only file-editing tools today, so the names never reach the journal. Collecting them is a change to the adapters, not to this dashboard.

**Acceptance is two different measures.** The rate above is whether an edit applied without erroring. Whether a human *kept* the work is the evidence split to the left: `intersected` means the agent's exact lines survived into the commit; `observed` means the file was edited but the text had changed before committing.
